title: When the Lantern Falls
premise: In the river town of Vellacourt, on the eve of revolution, Marguerite Quintana cuts type in their father's print shop and has learned that silence is the only currency the powerful respect. When the army requisitions the town and seizes a ledger of names belonging to the executed printer's circle, Marguerite discovers their own family's names among them and realizes the victors' historians will decide who the dead were. Racing to reprint the true record before the press is confiscated and the witnesses scattered, Marguerite must choose between protecting a brother who informed to save them and honoring the truth that will destroy him. The book ends with the pamphlet smuggled onto the river the night the town burns — the record survives, but Marguerite loses the family it was meant to save.
about_author: Dominic Thornbury is the pen name of a former archival restorer who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated printing records from provincial European archives. Their novels examine how ordinary tradespeople become accidental custodians of history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Letters
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. In the Quintana print shop, Marguerite cuts type by lamplight while their father teaches them which orders to refuse and which silences to keep. A neighbor's son disappears after a pamphlet circulates. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine — the reader learns the rules of survival in Vellacourt.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The army arrives to requisition the town; officers seize the ledger of names from the printers' mutual-aid circle, including the Quintana entry. Marguerite's brother Tomás, a clerk for the garrison, helped translate the requisition order. Emotional beat: betrayal surfaces as a small, deniable act.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Floorboards
chapters.summary: Father Quintana's POV. The father reveals the ledger was a decoy — the true names were hidden in a misprinted sheet only a type cutter would notice. He begins teaching Marguerite to read the errors, but a cough he has hidden all autumn worsens. Emotional beat: inheritance of a dangerous craft, and of a dying man's urgency.

chapters.title: The Historian's Assistant
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Captain Delorme, a scholar-official compiling the army's official account, interviews Marguerite about the shop's records. Marguerite performs ignorance while realizing Delorme is not cruel — merely certain that history belongs to the victors. Emotional beat: the seduction of safety offered by the powerful.

chapters.title: Tomás's Signature
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Tomás discovers his own signature authorized the requisition of the misprinted sheet, making him the instrument of his family's exposure. He weighs confessing to Marguerite against destroying the order. Emotional beat: shame curdling into rationalization — how a loyal son becomes an informer.

chapters.title: The Widow of Rue Basse
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite seeks out Séraphine, widow of the executed pamphleteer, the only living witness who can verify the names. Séraphine agrees to testify in print but demands the whole truth, including the Quintanas' compromises. Emotional beat: the cost of a record that spares no one.

chapters.title: A Press Runs at Night
chapters.summary: Father Quintana's POV. The family reassembles a hidden press in the cellar and begins setting the true account, Marguerite cutting type from memory of the hidden sheet. Tomás, guilt-ridden, brings them garrison paper and schedules. Emotional beat: fragile, feverish hope — the family briefly united by the work.

chapters.title: Delorme's Draft
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite obtains Delorme's official history draft and finds their father named a collaborator and Séraphine's husband a bandit. Delorme, confronted, admits he writes what the command requires. Emotional beat: cold clarity — justice will not come from the men writing the record.

chapters.title: The Night the Town Burns
chapters.summary: Tomás's POV. Retreating soldiers fire the town; the garrison orders the shop destroyed. Tomás confesses everything to his father, who forgives him and dies in the burning house protecting the type forms. Tomás carries the finished pamphlet to the river. Emotional beat: grief and atonement fused in one act of delivery.

chapters.title: Set in Lasting Metal
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On the far bank, Marguerite and Séraphine distribute the pamphlet to travelers and rivermen, letting the true record travel where the victors' historians cannot follow. Tomás surrenders himself to the new authorities, and Marguerite lets him go. Emotional beat: hard-won peace — truth survives, but at the price the ledger always promised.
